notes: Closes BACKLOG #28, surfaced by provider-health-probe-gaps. All 15 fallback rungs across all 4 agents are provider:openrouter, so a real OpenRouter outage stops every agent at once. Blocking sub-defect found while scoping: GROQ_API_KEY is exported only from ~/.bashrc, and systemd user units do not inherit an interactive shell env — the live journal shows '⚪ groq: not configured' on every tick while an interactive run shows '🟢 groq: up'. So Groq was unusable in the one environment where fallback matters. Fix, in order: (1) add GROQ_API_KEY to ~/.hermes/.env (0600, already loaded by every sdlc-sched-* unit via EnvironmentFile), (2) append llama-3.3-70b-versatile as the LAST rung for all 4 agents, (3) guard tests for cross-provider coverage and known-model resolution. Ordering is a correctness requirement: findHealthyFallback() skips only 'down', so an unkeyed rung is 'not-configured', still eligible, and would be selected during an outage then fail at call time. Gemini/Cerebras deliberately excluded — no keys on this host, so they would be the same false-assurance trap. VERIFIED: scheduler journal now reports groq: up (227ms) — checked from journalctl after a real timer run, not an interactive shell. No swap while OpenRouter healthy; all 4 agents on their configured models. Guard test confirmed non-vacuous (would flag all 4 agents without the rung). npm test 165/165, model-manager suite 56/56 (2 new). No secret staged — ~/.hermes/.env is outside the repo, mode 0600.
